title: The mailbox and the request logs, the system of the United States, and the records of provision
text: The Privacy Policy says that the operator's mailbox at iCloud Mail is provided to users in Japan by iTunes K.K., a company in Japan, which Sophaxis treats as entrusted with it, so that it is not a provision to a third party in a foreign country and no consent is asked of the people who write; that Apple Inc. may handle the emails in the United States; and that Vercel's request logs are not personal information for Sophaxis, with the reasons. It now gives the Personal Information Protection Commission's own information on the system of the United States, what Anthropic says of its measures, and why the measures of OpenAI and xAI cannot be given. It names docs/records-of-provision.md, which gives each recipient's name and address, as part of the record of provision to third parties, kept for at least three years. None of these narrows a right or adds a duty.

title: Why the rules on sending users' information do not apply, Sophaxis as the sender of its records, and the texts fetched again
text: The Privacy Policy says why the operator considers that the rules of Japan's Telecommunications Business Act on sending users' information outside do not apply: Sophaxis charges for nothing and earns nothing, so it runs no telecommunications business. The Takedown Policy says that, for the record pages and the PDF copies, Sophaxis is itself the sender under Japan's Act on providers of specified telecommunications services, so it does not rely on that Act's limitation of liability, and the operator is liable as Japanese law provides. The texts that the policies quote were fetched again on 2026-11-12, and the Privacy and Submission Policies now quote Article 1 of Russia's Federal Law No. 152-FZ. None of these narrows a right or adds a duty.

title: A first sentence for each policy, the steps while the operator cannot work, and numbers in the Japanese translations
text: Each policy now opens with a sentence that says what it is. The Terms of Use set out, under Continuity, what happens while the operator cannot work at all: who is told, what is paused, what stays online, what still works without the operator, and who could take over. The Japanese translations write durations and dates in Arabic digits, as the English does. None of these narrows a right or adds a duty.

title: How the criteria for listing change, a feed for policy changes, and no counts of views
text: The Moderation Policy says how the criteria for listing are reviewed and changed: at least once a year and when a law or a service changes, under the same rules as every other policy, with 14 days' notice for a change that narrows what can be listed. The Terms of Use say that each change to a policy is entered in this feed, which carries nothing else. The Privacy Policy says that no page shows a count of views or downloads, and that Sophaxis keeps no such count. None of these narrows a right or adds a duty.

title: Changes announced on the top page, before this feed began
text: Changes to these policies were announced on the top page before this feed began. They take effect in steps, from 2026-11-21 to 2026-11-25, as the notice on the top page and each policy say.

title: The feed begins
text: Each of the eight policies was last changed on 2026-11-11. Earlier versions, and every change to them, are kept in the history of the public repository. From this day, each change to a policy is also entered here.
